about: Cargo 1's main story, rewritten. Amendments replace the text of the chapters and endings the game already has; the game plays the new nodes from the story. The three endings are three births: the Hauler Hansa (trade), the Terran Mandate's first legion (combat), the course home to the Gyrotron (discovery).

hansa_founder.about: the captain minted the first Hansa Mark and signed the charter first

hansa_member.about: the captain signed the Hansa charter, not first

hansa_outside.about: the captain stayed out of the Hansa

carried_the_samples.about: the captain hauled the builders' metal to the Stellar Institute

hansa.charter.title: The charter
text: Eleven captains meet in a cargo hold at Epsilon because it is the only room nobody charges for.

The proposal fits on one sheet: the haulers pool their cargo, set their own rates, and settle in a coin nobody can print more of. A pellet of iridium and osmium, stamped with the weight it stands for. A Mark.
Someone has to put up the first metal and sign first. Everyone looks at the captain with the most routes.

choices.say: Put up the metal and sign first
Sign, but let someone else go first

trail.samples.title: Samples for the Stellar Institute
text: {ancient_scholar} has found the same grey alloy in comet ice at DSO-Gamma (Scholz's Star), in the collision dust at Theta III (Fomalhaut) and in a crate of Gamma tailings sold as scrap.
She wants one sample from each, delivered to the Stellar Institute at TRAPPIST-1, forty light-years out, by someone who will not sell them on the way. Her budget covers fuel and one hot meal.

trail.home.title: The course home
text: {ancient_scholar.short} sends you the course she worked out from the samples: back along Scholz's Star's track, to the far edge of our own system, near Sedna's orbit.
'If you want to see the ring before anyone else,' she writes, 'it is there now. It has been there the whole time.'

ch1.title: Deadhead
text: One ship, one loan, one empty hold. Haulers call that flying deadhead.
Five systems are close enough to reach before you retire: Alpha, Beta, Gamma, Delta, Epsilon. Buy where it is cheap, sell where it is not, and keep up the payments.

ch2a.title: Routes
text: Your name is on manifests in five systems now.
Every dock charges its own fee and every dock master has a cousin in customs. The older captains have started talking about pooling cargo and setting their own rates. They need someone with routes.
notes: balance: plot points ran far above every threshold; the endings now also need their arc's turning point

ch2b.title: Contract Iron
text: The corporations noticed that you shoot straight.
OmniCorp, Stellar Dynamics and the Xylo Consortium each keep a security legion, and each legion is short of pilots. The contracts pay well. Read them twice.
notes: balance: plot points ran far above every threshold; the endings now also need their arc's turning point

ch3a.title: The Mark
text: Money in the near systems is whatever the nearest bank says it is this week.
Haulers want something heavier: a coin that is also a receipt for mass carried. Somebody has to mint the first one and make every dock accept it.
notes: balance: plot points ran far above every threshold; the endings now also need their arc's turning point

ch3b.title: Legion
text: Three corporate legions, one pilot shortage, and you.
The corporations are talking about merging their security forces under one command. Everyone wants to know whose side your guns are on before the merger, not after.
notes: balance: plot points ran far above every threshold; the endings now also need their arc's turning point

ch3c.title: Builders' Metal
text: The research colonies keep finding the same grey alloy where nothing should have been made: comet ice, collision dust, mine tailings.
It was machined, and it is very old. The scholars who study it cannot afford careful haulers, so they are hoping for you.

ending_trade.title: The Hauler Hansa
text: The Hauler Hansa
The first Mark is a pellet of iridium and osmium with the first signer's ship registry stamped on it.
Every dock in the five systems accepts it. A clerk at Alpha files the charter under 'temporary'. It is still in that folder a century later.

The first Mark is a pellet of iridium and osmium with your ship's registry stamped on it. Haulers will carry that number in their pockets for a hundred years.
Every dock in the five systems accepts it. A clerk at Alpha files the charter under 'temporary'. It is still in that folder a century later.

ending_combat.title: The First Legion
text: The First Legion
The three corporate legions merge under one flag and one command, and your name heads its roll of pilots.
They call it the Terran Security Mandate. Within forty years the word 'Security' is dropped, and nobody remembers voting on that.

ending_discovery.title: The Heading
text: The Heading
The builders' metal was never scattered. It was a ring, the ring went round our own Sun, and Scholz's Star pulled a piece of it away when it passed 70,000 years ago.
You file the course home with the colonies' archive: from Scholz's Star, back along its track, to the far edge of our own system.
Nobody opens the file for forty years.

tycoon_offer.text: Every planet, asteroid base and outpost trades through a market you own. A courier offers you a coordinate for 1,500 credits: 'where the old metal goes when it moves'. Retire as Galactic Tycoon, or pay and fly there.

text: You are the Galactic Tycoon!
Congratulations, {player_name}! You have achieved the rank of {rank}.
You retire to the most expensive drum on Barnard's Star and complain about the prices.

stellar_portal.title: The Stellar Portal
text: The coordinate leads to a ring segment the size of a small moon, turning slowly, lit from inside.
Your navigation computer reports the date three times and gets three different answers.
On the far side the stars are where they should be. The prices are not.
